Route 5 (subscale block structure) run over the study's own PLOS S1 .sav, 1117 complete cases on ei1..ei16 (the live IRW table is a by-name melt of exactly these columns; irw::irw_table_sets() confirms the live item set is those 16 codes). The same authors publish the WLEIS-S under two rival numberings and the shipped mapping had to choose: SHIPPED interleaved UMA-form numbering (SEA 1,5,9,13; OEA 2,6,10,14; UOE 3,7,11,15; ROE 4,8,12,16) gives within-subscale mean r = 0.526 vs between-subscale 0.401 (gap +0.125) with 33/48 of items' top-3 correlates inside their own subscale; the RIVAL blocked Psicothema-Table-1 numbering (SEA 1-4 ... ROE 13-16) gives 0.432 vs 0.425 (gap +0.007) with 9/48. The OEA block is the clearest: ei2-ei6 .54, ei6-ei14 .60, ei10-ei14 .59, ei2-ei14 .52 against a .39 grand mean; the ROE block likewise ei8-ei16 .66, ei4-ei8 .59, ei12-ei16 .54. Corroborating: cross-subscale ADJACENT pairs (i,i+1) average r = 0.461 against 0.390 for cross-subscale non-adjacent pairs (n=15 vs 81), the proximity excess expected if ei1..ei16 is the form's printed presentation sequence. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: it pins each item's subscale (16/16) and eliminates the blocked numbering outright, but it is invariant to any permutation WITHIN a subscale -- swapping ei1 with ei9 (both SEA) would leave every number above unchanged. No per-item statistics are published for this sample (the 2016 paper reports only the EI total, M=4.98 SD=0.93), no reverse-keyed items exist to run route 6, all 16 items share one 1-7 scale so route 2 does not apply, and there is no marker item. PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.

route: 2 (per-item response-range/option-count structure) + 8 (semantic coherence of the response distribution)
evidence: Route 2, live per-item structure from irw::irw_table_sets(per_item=TRUE) against the SBQ-R's printed option counts: sbq1 6 levels 1-6 (instrument item 1 has 6 options, 1..6), sbq2 5 levels 1-5 (item 2 has 5), sbq3 6 levels 0-5 = the 5 options of item 3 plus 2 stray 0s, sbq4 7 levels 0-6 (item 4 is the only item numbered from 0, with 7 options). sbq1 is the only 6-option item and sbq4 the only 0-based 7-level one, so both are pinned outright. Corollary pinned by the same numbers: resp is the RAW option index, not SBQ-R scoring, which would give sbq1 4 levels and sbq3 3; the deposit's SuicideBehaviours_Scores equals the raw four-item sum for all 960 complete rows and maxes at 19 vs the published 3-18. What this does NOT establish: sbq2 and sbq3 are structurally identical 5-option 1-5 items and route 2 cannot separate them. Route 8 argues the direction only: among the 763 respondents answering sbq1=1 (never ideated or attempted, lifetime), 7 (0.9%) exceed level 1 on sbq2 -- a strict contradiction if sbq2 is past-year ideation -- against 27 (3.5%) on sbq3, which is possible if sbq3 is 'ever told someone'; and the level counts run 835/79/36/8/3 on sbq2 (monotone, as a frequency ladder should) vs 833/79/19/17/11 on sbq3 (flat tail, as item 3's paired 2a/2b, 3a/3b options should). Suggestive, not decisive, so PARTIAL rather than VERIFIED. Deposit per-item non-missing n (961/961/961) equals live n exactly, so the .sav is a faithful proxy. Re-runnable as verify_extremera_2016_sbq.R (VERDICT: PASS).

route: 3 (published/derived scoring rule reproduced) + 6 (keying polarity) + 8 (semantic distribution, secondary)
evidence: The source .sav's own derived score Happiness_Scores (SPSS label 'Felicidad Subjetiva') is reproduced exactly by (shs1+shs2+shs3+(8-shs4))/4 on 1124 of 1125 rows; reversing shs1 instead matches 182/1125, shs2 189/1125, shs3 217/1125, and reversing nothing 185/1125. The administered questionnaire's printed rule is 'Contrabalancear puntuaciones del item 4 (4r); Felicidad subjetiva total = (1+2+3+4r)/4', so this pins shs4 = questionnaire item 4 (the reverse-worded 'Algunas personas suelen ser muy poco felices...' item). Consistent with that, shs4 correlates -0.258/-0.223/-0.266 with shs1/shs2/shs3 while those three correlate +0.671/+0.588/+0.587 among themselves, so the items are stored raw. Secondary and non-decisive: shs2 has the largest midpoint mass (26.6% at resp=4 vs 17.4% shs1, 19.4% shs3, mean 4.77 vs 4.99/4.86), as expected of the peer-comparison item. What this does NOT establish: any sum over shs1/shs2/shs3 is invariant to permuting them, so the assignment of item 1 vs 2 vs 3 rests on the trailing digit of the authors' own column names and on the midpoint-mass hint, not on a statistic that separates all three -- hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. Re-runnable as verify_extremera_2016_shs.R (VERDICT: PASS).

Route 3 (published totals) over the 1123 complete cases in the live table, item metric (sum/5): live mean 4.254 vs published 4.25, live SD 1.272 vs 1.27, live Cronbach alpha 0.829 vs published .83 (Table 1, an image, read directly). Convergent correlations against the sibling IRW tables from the same respondents: r(SWLS, extremera_2016_ei mean) live +0.385 vs published .38; r(SWLS, extremera_2016_sbq mean) live -0.282 vs published -.28. Direction control: the reversed 1-7 anchor assignment gives a mean of 3.746, missing the published 4.25 by 0.504 on a 1-7 metric and flipping the sign of both correlations, so the option_text<->resp axis (1=Strongly disagree .. 7=Strongly agree) and raw, unreversed storage are pinned. Route 7 (marker item): per-item corrected item-total r = swls1 0.644, swls2 0.657, swls3 0.742, swls4 0.645, swls5 0.492, and per-item SD = 1.564, 1.512, 1.557, 1.616, 1.962 -- swls5 is simultaneously the minimum item-total and the maximum SD, the SWLS literature's stable signature of item 5 ("If I could live my life over...", Diener et al. 1985 loading .61 against .72-.84 for items 1-4), so swls5 is pinned. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: swls1..swls4 are not distinguished from one another. A sum/alpha is invariant to permutation, the paper publishes no per-item statistics, all five items share one 1-7 scale (route 2 unavailable), there is one unidimensional subscale (route 5 unavailable) and no reverse-keyed item (route 6 unavailable); and the item-total profile only weakly tracks the 1985 loadings overall (Spearman 0.564, with swls3 above swls1 where the loadings tie). Those four rest on the source .sav column numbering matching canonical SWLS order. PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.

route: script re-run: per-item non-missing counts vs irw_table_sets per-item n; plus per-item resp-range structure
evidence: Re-ran data/face_memory_test.R's code-assignment logic over the deposit's data.csv (1768 rows) and compared predicted non-missing counts (-1 and 0 -> NA) against live per-item n from irw_table_sets(per_item=TRUE): 175/175 exact, e.g. item 1=Q1 1759 vs 1759, item 75=Q75 1768 vs 1768, item 76=PQ1 199 vs 199, item 175=PQ100 184 vs 184. Response-range signature agrees: items 1-75 are all 1-2 (face old/new), items 76-175 all 1-5 (HEXACO agreement). This pins the two-instrument block boundary and the within-block offset jointly. It does NOT separate every item from every other item: only 19 of 175 have an n unique across the table, so a swap between two items sharing the same n (e.g. the many face items at n=1764) would be invisible to this route; per-item means would need a full export. PARTIAL, and moot for shipping in any case -- no item text was written, the table is blocked on rights (HEXACO half) and on image-only stimuli (face half).

Route 5 (subscale block structure) + route 8 (mean-level profile) + route 7 (marker item), all computed on the CC0 source file the IRW table is melted from (n=262; item codes are the source column names, so the codes cannot have shifted). (a) Convergent/discriminant: within-block mean r Depression 0.419, Anxiety 0.370, Stress 0.461; between-block D-A 0.303, D-S 0.397, A-S 0.351 -- every block is more coherent internally than with either other block. The weaker global form does NOT hold (Anxiety within 0.370 < D-S 0.397), which is the DASS's known general-distress factor rather than a mapping defect, and it is why this route is underpowered here in the same way route 5 was for alsuhibani_2022_gcbs. (b) Subscale means Stress 1.369 > Depression 1.064 > Anxiety 0.824, the standard non-clinical DASS-21 profile. (c) Marker: DASS-21 item 17 ("I felt I wasn't worth much as a person") is the least endorsed of the seven depression items at 0.576, against 0.973-1.424 for the rest -- as it must be in a working, non-clinical sample. Documentary evidence not re-tested by the script: the deposit's DDI column order places the codes under three all-null section headers DEPRESSI/ANXIETY/STRESS in exactly the canonical DASS-21 partition (chance 2.5e-9). WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the order of the seven items WITHIN a block. Swapping the item_text of Q3_A and Q5_A (both depression) leaves every number above unchanged, and route 1 is unavailable because no paper reporting per-item statistics for this sample could be found. Route 2 does not apply (all 21 items share the 0-3 scale) and route 6 does not apply (the DASS-21 has no reverse-keyed items). PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.
